verses.speaker: Arjuna
skt: तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव
verses.tr: Arjuna said: Janardana, if you think knowledge is better than action, then why do you push me into this terrible action, Keshava?

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: Your words seem mixed and confuse my mind. Tell me clearly the one way by which I can reach the highest good.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: The Lord said: As I said before, there are two paths in this world: the path of knowledge for those who reflect, and the path of action for those who work.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: A person does not become free from action just by not starting any work, nor reach perfection just by giving things up.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: No one can stay without acting even for a moment; everyone is made to act, whether they like it or not, by the qualities of nature.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन्
verses.tr: One who holds back the body from action but keeps thinking about pleasures in the mind is fooling himself and is called a hypocrite.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: But one who controls the senses with the mind and, without attachment, uses the body for selfless action, is far better, Arjuna.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः
verses.tr: Do your duty, for action is better than inaction. Without action you could not even keep your body alive.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Action binds people, except action done as an offering (yajna). So, son of Kunti, work in that spirit, free from attachment.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: In the beginning, the Creator made beings along with yajna and said: "Through this you will flourish; let it give you all you wish for."

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Nourish the gods with this, and let the gods nourish you. Caring for each other, you will reach the highest good.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः
verses.tr: Pleased by yajna, the gods will give you what you need. One who enjoys their gifts without giving anything back is really a thief.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात्
verses.tr: Good people who eat what is left after offering are freed from all wrongs; but those who cook only for themselves are eating sin.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Living beings come from food, food comes from rain, rain comes from yajna, and yajna comes from action.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Know that action comes from the Veda, and the Veda comes from the Imperishable. So the all-pervading Brahman is always present in yajna.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: One who does not keep this wheel turning, living selfishly and only for the senses, lives in vain, Arjuna.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते
verses.tr: But one who delights in the Self, is satisfied in the Self and content in the Self alone, has nothing more that must be done.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Such a person gains nothing by acting and loses nothing by not acting, and does not depend on anyone for anything.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: So always do the work that needs to be done, without attachment. By working without attachment, a person reaches the Supreme.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: King Janaka and others reached perfection through action. You too should act, if only for the good of the world.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Whatever a great person does, others follow. Whatever standard they set, the world goes by it.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन
verses.tr: Arjuna, there is nothing in the three worlds that I have to do, and nothing I lack or need to gain; yet I keep working.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः
verses.tr: For if I ever stopped working tirelessly, people everywhere would follow my example.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम्
verses.tr: If I did not act, these worlds would fall apart; I would cause confusion and ruin all these beings.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: As the ignorant work with attachment, Arjuna, so should the wise work without attachment, wishing for the good of the world.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: The wise should not unsettle people who are attached to their work. Instead, working steadily themselves, they should inspire others to do their work well.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: All actions are carried out by the qualities of nature, but a person confused by ego thinks, "I am the doer."

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते
verses.tr: But one who knows the truth about the gunas and their work, strong-armed one, sees that "the gunas are acting on the gunas" and does not get attached.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: People confused by nature's qualities become attached to their workings. Those who understand fully should not unsettle those who understand only in part.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Offering all your actions to me, with your mind on the Self, free from desire and from "mine," fight without the fever of grief.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Those who always follow this teaching of mine with faith, without finding fault, are also freed from the bonds of action.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: But those who find fault with my teaching and do not follow it are confused about all knowledge; know them to be lost and without understanding.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति
verses.tr: Even the wise act according to their own nature. All beings follow their nature; what can forcing it achieve?

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Liking and disliking for the things of the senses are natural; but do not fall under their control, for they are obstacles on your path.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Better is your own duty, even done imperfectly, than someone else's duty done well. Better to die doing your own duty; another's duty is full of danger.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
skt: अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः
verses.tr: Arjuna said: Then what drives a person to do wrong, Krishna, even against their will, as if forced?

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: The Lord said: It is desire, and it is anger, born of rajas. It can never be satisfied and leads to great wrong. Know it as the enemy here.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: As fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and an unborn child by the womb, so is knowledge covered by desire.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Knowledge is covered by this constant enemy of the wise, desire, which burns like a fire that is never satisfied, Arjuna.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: The senses, the mind and the intellect are where desire lives. Through them it hides knowledge and confuses the soul.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: So, best of the Bharatas, first bring your senses under control, and then destroy this troublemaker that ruins knowledge and wisdom.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः
verses.tr: The senses are said to be higher than the body; higher than the senses is the mind; higher than the mind is the intellect; and higher than the intellect is the Self.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Knowing the Self to be higher than the intellect, and steadying the mind by the Self, strong-armed one, defeat this enemy called desire, so hard to conquer.
